pr_title: Fix synchronization of global class name
pr_body: This should fix the issues #76380, #75388, #81615 and #92054 This should manage these situations: - At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg is missing or incomplete but the filesystem cache is present - At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg and the system cache are missing - At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg is missing classes but are present on disk - At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg has a class that does not exists on disk - At startup, the path for class name in global_script_class_cache.cfg has changed - In the editor if the user duplicates a script with a class name and change the class name after - In the editor if the user changes the class name for an existing class name and change it again - In the editor if the user deletes a folder containing a script with a class name that is used by another script - Exporting project from command line that uses global class names in addons without or with an invalid global_script_class_cache.cfg - Updating scripts from outside the Editor that uses new global class name The global class name are now loaded from the scripts at the editor startup, always recreating the global_script_class_cache.cfg. When not in the editor, the global_script_class_cache.cfg is used for performance when the project runs. Bugsquad edit: - Fix #76380 - Fix #75388 - Fix #81615 - Fix #92054 Edited: Adding modifications for the issue #81615 Edited: Updating for the modifications loading class name at startup from scripts. Edited: Adding modifications for the issue #92054 Edited: Adding fix for deletion of folders

While I'm sure this change will be of help to many people, since it does seem to resolve the issue of scripts ending up in a perpetual state of error and needing to be resaved one at a time, it obviously does not change the actual order of `global_script_class_cache.cfg` being populated after the initial load of the autoloads, so you'll still see errors from that initial broken compilation of any autoloads that reference any `class_name`, although it will (mostly) only output to the command-line (i.e. `stderr`) with this change, since `EditorLog` has yet to initialize when autoloads are first loaded.

This does however mean that importing from the command-line using `--headless`, through something like a CI job, either explicitly through the new `--import` option or implicitly through `--export-debug`/`--export-release`, will still emit errors. I'm able to reproduce this by exporting the repro project in #75388 for example, even with the latest commit as of this comment.

There's also the issue of the more or less official (and fairly common) [plugin pattern](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/plugins/editor/making_plugins.html#registering-autoloads-singletons-in-plugins) where you have a `@tool` script that registers a potentially new autoload using `add_autoload_singleton` in its `_enter_tree`. In such a case `add_autoload_singleton` will trigger `update_autoload`, which kicks off another broken (assuming it depends on some other `class_name`) autoload compilation, which this time actually emits to the editor log, since `EditorLog` is up and running by that point. You'll see that in this repro that I just made: [autoload-plugin-errors.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15436861/autoload-plugin-errors.zip)

Both of these are of course largely "cosmetic" issues (as far as I can tell), since these errors seem to eventually get dealt with by your `recompile_invalid_autoload_scripts`, but any non-trivial project that uses `class_name` or a plugin autoload (like [GodotLogger](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/1975)) in a widespread manner will still end up with hundreds/thousands of errors in these two scenarios if there's no valid `global_script_class_cache.cfg`.

Anyway, again, I'm not saying this change shouldn't be merged, and I wouldn't/shouldn't be the judge of that in the first place, but I figured I'd bring this up in case it hadn't been considered already, or if there's some discussion to be had about a more holistic solution.

I did a review and I am not very found of the approach. The manual filesystem scan in ScriptServer is likely overkill. EditorFileSystem is specially optimized to only scan files and directories that change, which allows for the editor to remain snappy even with very large projects. This PR goes against that.

The way I would solve this is directly inside EditorFileSystem by having a more layered way to scan the files. Probably something like:


1. Scan all changes
2. Instead of doing changes immediately, build a list of things that changed.
3. Pre process scripts first in the list.
4. Process everything else.

> EditorFileSystem is specially optimized to only scan files and directories that change, which allows for the editor to remain snappy even with very large projects.

Eh, that's not entirely true. FileSystemDock rescans all files on pretty much every operation. It's nice that EditorFileSystem was designed this way, but it's not used this way.

I just pushed a new version for this PR following the recommendation of @reduz.

### Modifications:
- This new version reverts all the modifications in ScriptServer and puts the management of the `global_script_class_cache.cfg` back in ProjectSettings.
- All scans are now done directly in EditorFileSystem as it should be.
- The loading of autoloads and plugins have been moved to the first scan.
- The first part of the first scan is done in the new method `_first_scan_filesystem`.
- `_scan_new_dir` only discovers the directories and files and calculates the file types.
- A new method `_process_file_system` validates the files and creates actions for updates/reimportations. It has two modes:
  - Script Only: Used in `_first_scan_filesystem` to process only scripts to load global class names.
  - All: Processes all the files. This mode is used after the global class names, autoloads, and plugins are loaded.
- The progress bar in FileSystemDock has been fixed while processing files on startup.

### Algorithm:
- On the first scan, call `_first_scan_filesystem`:
  - Discover all the files (`_scan_new_dir`).
  - Process all the scripts  (`_process_file_system` in Script Only mode).
  - Load autoloads.
  - Load plugins.
  - If new importers have been added:
    - Rediscover all the files (`_scan_new_dir`): new extensions or resource types could have been added/updated from custom importers.
    - Process all the discovered files (`_process_file_system`).

- On subsequent full scans (ex: renaming files):
  - Discover all the files (`_scan_new_dir`).
  - Process all the discovered files (`_process_file_system`).


### Test cases
It took me a while but I retested all these test cases with different MRP from issues:
- At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg is missing or incomplete but the filesystem cache is present
- At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg and the system cache are missing
- At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg is missing classes but are present on disk
- At startup, the global_script_class_cache.cfg has a class that does not exists on disk
- At startup, the path for class name in global_script_class_cache.cfg has changed
- In the editor if the user duplicates a script with a class name and change the class name after
- In the editor if the user changes the class name for an existing class name and change it again
- In the editor if the user deletes a folder containing a script with a class name that is used by another script
- Exporting project from command line that uses global class names in addons without or with an invalid global_script_class_cache.cfg
- Updating scripts from outside the Editor that uses new global class name

issue_context.title: Pulling GDScript changes that introduce a new `class_name` results in errors
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.3.dev [bd2300d77]

### System information

Windows 11 (10.0.22631)

### Issue description

This is tangentially related to #75388, except this issue does not necessarily need to involve autoloads or plugins.

When you're doing something like pulling in changes to your project from another Git repository, and those changes contain a new GDScript class with a `class_name`, which is then used in another GDScript file (existing or otherwise) you will be met with errors like this:

```
res://main.gd:5 - Parse Error: Identifier "SomeNewThing" not declared in the current scope.
modules\gdscript\gdscript.cpp:2895 - Failed to load script "res://main.gd" with error "Parse error". (User)
```

If you then reload the current project, you'll find that everything parses just fine.

The reason for this seems quite simple. Scripts are loaded and fully parsed as part of `EditorFileSystem::_update_scan_actions`, and the updating of the global `class_name` cache happens as part of `EditorFileSystem::_update_pending_script_classes`, which happens after `_update_scan_actions`, as seen [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/bd2300d77a6008167043f23fd91bcc562cde0a19/editor/editor_file_system.cpp#L1278-L1279).

So the global `class_name` cache would presumably need to be updated before scripts are fully parsed somehow.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP.
2. Once loaded, run `git checkout b64a4b4dd`.
3. Note the errors shown in the editor's Output pane.
4. Reload the project.
5. Note the absence of any errors.

(To go back to the initial commit, do `git checkout f4f9e9d17`.)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[ClassNamePullErrors.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/15353961/ClassNamePullErrors.zip)
